title: Epochal soft-residency and hot-slab reuse controller
author: Maya Srinivasan
description: Motivation: Mixed tail-heavy and throughput-heavy workloads expose two recurring issues in the paged KV layer: eviction/rehydration churn for transient hot prefixes and fragmentation driven by eager pinning. This PR introduces an epochal soft-residency model plus a hot-slab reuse controller to reduce churn, improve locality-aware reuse, and provide scheduling hints for the runtime to align batching and kernel selection. High level: 1) Epochal soft-residency: rather than hard pinning, pages gain a short-term 'soft residency' token on access that persists across a tunable epoch window (default 250ms). Tokens decay probabilistically across epochs using a jittered exponential decay seed so that bursty accesses keep residency while infrequent touches gracefully drop out. 2) Hot-slab reuse controller: per-slab lightweight counters track hotness with age buckets and allow controlled reuse of recently freed blocks to avoid immediate cross-slab allocations. The controller exposes an API to the block allocator to request a 'reuse lease' which biases allocations toward the hot slab pool for a small amortized cost. 3) Eviction credits and prefetch hints: requests that trigger evictions can optionally attach an eviction credit budget; the allocator uses credits to prefer lazy reclaim paths and to schedule low-cost prefetches for anticipated reaccess. 4) Scheduler integration: continuous-batching receives a batch-affinity tag that the runtime uses to co-schedule requests that likely share soft-residency, reducing KV cache misses and enabling kernel specialization for shorter KV lookups. 5) Telemetry and knobs: adds per-epoch metrics (soft_residency_hits, soft_residency_misses, reuse_lease_success, eviction_credit_spend) and a dynamic config endpoint to tune epoch window and reuse lease size. Backwards compatibility: behavior is off by default for Dedicated/Private control planes and gated via a feature flag for hosted until a gradual rollout. Summary of observed results: microbenchmarks (mixed chat + vector lookups) show 9-11% p99 generation latency reduction and 12% lower per-token kernel time due to fewer KV misses; long-running stress tests show reduced fragmentation (measured as 18% fewer cross-slab allocations over 6h). Rollout plan: feature-flag rollout on canary, then ramp across regions with telemetry checks. Links: Linear ENG-4532 for eviction-credits, ENG-4698 for batching affinity.
